original_question:
Schwartz class is the collection of all ∞-regular functions on R^n. Let A be an expansive dilation with integer entries (equivalently AZ^n ⊂ Z^n) and let Γ = Z^n.

Do Schwartz class wavelets exist for integer expansive dilations A and lattice Γ = Z^n?
target_in_paper: Section 3.5, Problem 3.5 (Meyer wavelets for integer dilations).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target: it matches Problem 3.5 almost verbatim. It correctly identifies the class of dilations (expansive with integer entries), the equivalent lattice-preservation condition A Z^n ⊂ Z^n, the lattice Γ = Z^n, and the localization class being the Schwartz class as discussed immediately before the problem.
missing_details: The paper’s notion of wavelet in this higher-dimensional section is relative to a pair (A, Γ) and, in general, may mean a finite collection Ψ = {ψ1, …, ψL}, not necessarily a single generator; this is set up in Definition 3.1.

To be stand-alone, the question should specify the ambient space L^2(R^n) and require that the affine system { |det A|^(j/2) ψl(A^j x − k) : l = 1, …, L; j ∈ Z; k ∈ Z^n } be an orthonormal basis of L^2(R^n).
The quantifier should be explicit: the paper is asking whether such Schwartz-class wavelets exist for every expansive integer dilation A, not merely for some particular A.

The surrounding context makes clear that one should allow multiple generators in higher dimensions; for integer expansive A, any well-localized orthonormal wavelet must have a number L of generators divisible by |det A| − 1.

If one unpacks the paper’s terminology, Schwartz class is identified there with the class of ∞-regular functions, where r-regular means Cr and all partial derivatives of order at most r have the decay stated just before Section 3.5.
The draft does not mention that the problem is already solved in dimensions 1 and 2 in the cited discussion; by Theorem 3.7, the remaining open case is dimensions n ≥ 3.
refined_question: For every expansive integer matrix A ∈ GLn(R) with A Z^n ⊂ Z^n—and hence, in the only unresolved range, for n ≥ 3—does there exist a finite orthonormal (A, Z^n)-wavelet Ψ = {ψ1, …, ψL} contained in the Schwartz class S(R^n) (equivalently, in the paper’s terminology, consisting of ∞-regular functions), i.e. such that the affine system { |det A|^(j/2) ψl(A^j x − k) : l = 1, …, L; j ∈ Z; k ∈ Z^n } is an orthonormal basis of L^2(R^n)?
justification: The draft is essentially the exact open problem stated in the paper: Section 3.5, Problem 3.5. To make it mathematically self-contained and faithful to the paper, the rewrite imports the definition of an orthonormal (A, Γ)-wavelet from Definition 3.1, keeps the hypothesis A Z^n ⊂ Z^n from (3.2), and makes explicit that higher-dimensional wavelets may require finitely many generators, as emphasized in the surrounding discussion on well-localized wavelets. I did not broaden the question to rational dilations, because the paper mentions that only as a possible further extension after stating Problem 3.5. I also sharpened the statement by noting that Theorem 3.7 settles the 2-dimensional case, so the genuinely open part is n ≥ 3.
